subject: SIG evidence: deployment allowlist, key custody & pipeline whitelist
messages:
From: Katie Barnes <katie@secureassure.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: security-assessor@finbank.com
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG request — deployment allowlist + key custody artifacts

Hi Soojin / Marissa,

Thanks for taking this — FinBank's SIG assessor is asking for a focused evidence bundle around deployment controls and key custody for the services that will handle customer PII. Specifically we need the following items scoped to the production cluster(s) serving FinBank: 

- current deployment allowlist / approved images (container digests or image tags)
- admission controller policy snapshot (OPA/Gatekeeper / Kyverno rules)
- KMS/HSM custody proof (rotation logs, access list for custodians)
- CI/CD pipeline allowlist / trusted runner matrix
- changelog or approval history for any production infra changes in last 90 days

We have a short turnaround: assessor would like to review by EOD Monday (2027-05-17). Can you confirm what you can provide and any blockers? Attaching a checklist worksheet to help map artifacts to SIG questions.

Attachment: sig_checklist_deployment_kms_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 94KB)

Best,
Katie Barnes
Senior Assessor — SecureAssure
katie@secureassure.com

---
From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Katie Barnes <katie@secureassure.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG request — deployment allowlist + key custody artifacts

Katie — thanks for the checklist and clear scope. We can supply the majority of these artifacts; here is the plan and owners: 

- Deployment allowlist (image digests + admission exceptions): owner Karthik, ETA Mon 2027-05-17 morning.
- Admission controller policies (Gatekeeper constraints + snapshots): owner Monica, ETA Mon 2027-05-17.
- KMS/HSM custody and rotation logs: I'll pull rotation CSV and the access policy export; note that HSM-backed keys are managed via internal KMS and an HSM provider — we'll provide masked audit lines where required. ETA Mon 2027-05-17 afternoon.
- CI/CD pipeline allowlist and runner whitelist matrix: Marissa will export signed pipeline policies and runner tags.
- Change approval history: we'll include the change request links and signed approvals for the 90-day window.

Two quick questions: 1) Do you need raw Git commit SHAs for resulting image builds, or is image digest + pipeline trace sufficient? 2) For HSM logs, do you need full principal identifiers, or can we provide redacted IDs + KMS audit UUIDs?

We will post artifacts to the secure evidence drive and share read-only links (Doc-level access). I will also attach a short narrative that maps each artifact to the SIG question number.

Thanks — assigning tasks and will keep you posted.

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Staff Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Attachment: action_plan_short.txt (plain text, 1.8KB)

---
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: Katie Barnes <katie@secureassure.com>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG request — deployment allowlist + key custody artifacts

Quick update and links to exported artifacts (provisionally redacted where policy requires):

Artifacts uploaded to: https://drive.redwood/repo/sig/evidence/FB-2027-0043 (read-only link provided to assessor)

Files included:
- pipeline_allowlist_20270510.yaml — approved images and pipeline allowlist (includes image digest -> pipeline job mapping).
- k8s_admission_policies_snapshot_20270509.json — Gatekeeper constraint templates + sample violation output.
- ci_cd_whitelist_matrix_20270511.pdf — signed runner whitelist and environment separation matrix.
- hsm_rotation_log_20270430.csv — exported rotation audit (principal IDs redacted to UUIDs per customer policy).
- change_approval_index_90d.csv — CR numbers, approver emails, timestamp, and brief justification.

Additional context:
- We keep automated signing of images in the pipeline; the allowlist YAML references the image signature metadata. If assessor requires raw cosign attestations, we can produce them but need a short lead (couple hours).
- For HSM custody, full principal names are restricted for privacy — we provide the KMS audit UUIDs and the HSM access policy export. If FinBank requests a non-redacted export under an NDA, we can escalate.

Attachments: pipeline_allowlist_20270510.yaml (YAML, 7KB); hsm_rotation_log_20270430.csv (CSV, 45KB)

I'll shepherd any follow-ups.

— Karthik
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

---
From: FinBank Security <security-assessor@finbank.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Katie Barnes <katie@secureassure.com>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG request — deployment allowlist + key custody artifacts

Team — thank you for the quick turnaround and the artifacts. We received the drive package and sampled the items listed below; initial observations: 

- pipeline_allowlist_20270510.yaml: contains clear mapping to signed image digests. Good — we may request a sample cosign attestation for one production image to validate the signing chain.
- k8s_admission_policies_snapshot_20270509.json: policies look complete; please also include a short note describing how policy exceptions are requested and approved (who signs off).
- hsm_rotation_log_20270430.csv: UUID approach is acceptable for our review; if we need non-redacted principals we will escalate to FinBank legal.
- ci_cd_whitelist_matrix_20270511.pdf: At a glance this matches our expectation for runner separation. One minor ask — can you provide a table mapping runner IDs to IAM roles?

Next steps: we'll collate a short follow-up with a couple of discrete asks (cosign sample, exception approval note, runner->IAM mapping). Please expect that as a tracker in SUP-4312. Thanks again for the clear file names and the change approval index — that made sampling straightforward.

Regards,
FinBank Security Review Team
security-assessor@finbank.com
